items.question: Why did he build the evaluation harness before the chat interface?
items.reply: **Shubham** built the evaluation harness before the chat interface because relying on whether an answer feels right is not a measurement, and it cannot tell whether a reranker justifies its latency or survive a change in chunking [1]. Once a chat interface exists, retrieval tends to be tuned by asking questions and seeing if the answers feel right, which makes it impossible to evaluate configurations objectively [1]. Building the eval harness first ensures that retrieval metrics and a faithfulness judge exist to produce numbers, so the final configuration is chosen on evidence rather than fitted to an already chosen UI [1].

items.question: Why did the scaled RFE model score differently from the unscaled one?
items.reply: The difference occurred because ordinary least squares is scale-invariant, meaning standardising the inputs cannot change R² on its own [1, 2, 3]. Instead, Recursive Feature Elimination ran separately on each matrix and selected a different set of eight features in each run [1, 2]. Specifically, the scaled run swapped a weekend flag and the number of distinct items for a subtotal and a second courier-load count [1, 2].

items.question: How did he sample the NYC taxi data?
items.reply: To handle dataset sizes of over 3 million trips per month that would not fit comfortably in memory on a laptop, Shubham sampled across all twelve months of 2023 rather than taking a single month whole [2, 6]. He processed each monthly Parquet file by extracting the date and hour from the pickup timestamp, and then used Pandas to sample 5 percent of the entries from each hour of each day [1]. That sampling process resulted in a working set of 489,542 trips [2, 5].

items.question: How does the notes app keep a user logged in securely?
items.reply: To keep a user logged in securely, **Shubham** uses JSON Web Tokens stored in secure HTTP-only cookies with strict cross-site request forgery protection [1]. A server-side hook runs before every request to read the session cookie, verify the JWT, and store the username on local request state while clearing any bad or expired tokens [2]. Passwords are also securely hashed using bcrypt during registration [6].
